items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: Is there anything else, Mrs. Lane, you could tell us about the old days when your husband had the bands?

ctx.x: That really played music. They said, fellas take it off, they don't take their socks off and shove it down. Yeah. That's all of that sort of stuff. Well, they used to play to miss them kids, you know. We were all youngsters then, you know. They were terrible. I had a handful to handle them. They were over home with her all the time, a whole bunch of them. I had a garret, a big open garret, you know. Had beds up in there. And when I'd take a job out of the city, I wouldn't trust them buggers. I'd make them come…
Is there anything else, Mrs. Lane, you could tell us about the old days when your husband had the bands? That you'd like to add?

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: Now, after I was married, you understand, she used to run the business for me.

ctx.x: You must have made quite a bit of money out of that then in those days, right?
Now, after I was married, you understand, she used to run the business for me. I wouldn't be home. I'd be out.
What year were you all married?

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: Coych and, uh, what's his name, mother?

ctx.x: He was, he was, uh, he used to call us up all the time, poor fella. He was so sick all the time. And he called me off. Okay.
I'm going to say Blottsy, Mississippi. Blottsy, Mississippi. Coych and, uh, West End Hose. Coych and, uh, what's his name, mother?
Hmm? Uh, Gussie Zinneman and, um, uh, what's his name?
